title: Ethiopia’s Nobel-Winning Leader Wins Big Again — But Not Everyone Is Cheering
summary: Did you know Ethiopia’s leader won the Nobel Peace Prize for ending a long fight with a neighbor? Now Abiy Ahmed has won another big election. His Prosperity Party took more than 90% of the seats in parliament, just like last time. That means he stays prime minister. Abiy became famous in 2018 when he freed journalists and political prisoners and let banned parties return. In 2019, he got the Nobel Peace Prize for making peace with Eritrea, a country next door. But some people say things have changed. Critics and human rights groups say his government now arrests journalists and shuts down groups that speak out. Ethiopia has also seen terrible violence. A civil war in the Tigray region from 2020 to 2022 caused hundreds of thousands of deaths. A peace deal was signed in 2022, but this May, Tigray’s leaders broke the deal by taking back control of the region’s government. That has experts worried about new fighting. Elections couldn’t even happen in Tigray because it wasn’t safe. In other regions like Oromia and Amhara, armed groups have taken over large areas. Still, Abiy’s government says the economy is growing fast — over 10% this year, one of the best in Africa. His party campaigned on better food security and economic success. But with so much unrest, many wonder if the peace prize winner can keep his country together.
why_it_matters: Even a leader who won the Nobel Peace Prize can face huge problems at home—this shows that running a country is very tricky, and that violence can hurt millions of kids just like you.

background_read: Ethiopia is an ancient country in East Africa and the second most populous nation on the continent.
Abiy Ahmed became prime minister in 2018 and surprised the world by making peace with Eritrea, a neighbor that Ethiopia once fought a long war with.
The Nobel Peace Prize is one of the highest honors anyone can receive, awarded to those who take big steps to stop conflicts.
Article_Structure: WHO: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed and his Prosperity Party.
WHAT: They won over 90% of the seats in parliament again, but the election could not happen safely in the war-torn Tigray region.
WHERE: Ethiopia, especially the regions of Tigray, Oromia, and Amhara where armed groups are active.
WHY: Abiy focused on economic growth and food security to win votes, even as critics worry about freedom and new violence.

perspectives.description: Many Ethiopians are happy with Abiy because he brought peace with Eritrea and the economy is growing faster than almost anywhere else in Africa.
Critics say Abiy's government now locks up journalists and shuts down groups that disagree, the very opposite of what made him famous in 2018.
Some experts think deep ethnic splits in Ethiopia mean that even a Nobel winner cannot easily stop armed uprisings and keep the nation united.
